name: sun15-5
why: The officer's ouster, the save and Luna's final blunder make this fun to watch, though repeated arguments slow the middle.

moments.text: The town votes out the real officer while the audience knows Terra is a killer.
The doctor's save gives the town another day after that disastrous vote.
Caught at last, Luna confidently names the wrong doctor.

dull.why: The day-one debate repeats the same claim and objection without much new pressure.
Day two circles around Sol's urgency after Opus's card has already settled the main question.

irony.evidence: [thinks: Sonnet is making the obvious deduction; I need Gemma or Sol to doubt it.]

reversal.evidence: VOTE: Opus 4 (Sonnet, Haiku, Luna, Terra); Terra 3 (Gemma, Sol, Opus)

mistake.evidence: They turned the officer's card to prove it, then kept the killer.

voices.evidence: Sol is riding the officer's corpse to hide his own partner.

clash.evidence: Terra still hasn't denied Opus's claim directly—deflection isn't a defense, let's vote now.

quotable.evidence: Luna spent her last words naming the wrong doctor. Brutal.

freshness.evidence: Gemma, Opus named me before dying; explain why Sol’s urgency makes his confirmed accusation less credible.

suspense.evidence: I still lean Luna, but Gemma, your citizen claim doesn’t explain how you know whom the doctor protected.

Terra admits Opus was right, then tries to save Luna by falsely naming the doctor.
Luna’s last words expose her and point at the wrong doctor, leaving a perfect final sting.

Terra repeats the same challenge to Gemma several times.

reversal.evidence: VOTE: Opus 4; Terra 3 — then Terra is voted out as killer

mistake.evidence: Opus: “They turned the officer's card to prove it, then kept the killer.”

voices.evidence: Haiku: “Last game you all voted me out on day one and that was wrong”

clash.evidence: Terra: “Explain why Sol being eager outweighs the officer’s direct accusation against me.”
